summary: We developed Junior Astronaut Training, an interactive educational game designed to introduce students, especially young learners, to the exciting world of space exploration and astronaut training. The project simulates a simplified astronaut training experience through engaging activities, challenges, and interactive tasks that help users understand the skills and knowledge required for space missions.
details:
What it does and how it works
Junior Astronaut Trainer is a browser-based 3D learning game. Players enter an astronaut name, choose a suit colour, and get a short briefing from their mission mentor, Kalpana. They then walk around a virtual Moon outpost using the keyboard and mouse (WASD to move, mouse to look, E to pick up or install, Q to drop, ESC to pause). The goal is to collect 18 pieces of equipment and install them in the right assembly bays to bring five systems online: solar power, water production, oxygen production, crew habitat and food cultivation. A mission panel tracks progress, an equipment library explains what each part does, and finishing all five systems earns a personalised certificate.

Benefits
Players learn what a Moon settlement needs by doing, not just reading. Each machine has a plain-language explanation, such as how a condenser turns water vapour into liquid or how a reactor separates oxygen from lunar soil. The game runs in a web browser, so nothing needs to be installed.

Intended impact
We want to make space-settlement ideas easier to explore, understand and discuss, and to inspire young learners to think about the engineering and science of living on the Moon.

Tools and technology
HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with the Three.js library for the 3D world. Visual Studio Code for writing the code, GitHub for storing it and GitHub Pages for hosting it online. Google Fonts for typography. It runs on a standard computer with a keyboard and mouse.

Creativity
The outpost is built entirely from code, with no downloaded 3D models. Players carry the solar array up a staircase to the roof, and a single action deploys radiation shielding on all four sides of the base. The game also has a guided mentor, a suit-colour choice and a certificate.

Factors we considered
We wrote the explanations in simple language for young learners. The current build is desktop-first, and mobile touch controls are a planned improvement. It is an educational prototype, not a real engineering design or a certified life-support system.
